run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The checkout service is completely down: its Deployment's pod template carries a nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node, a hostname no node in the cluster has, so both checkout pods are Pending/Unschedulable, the checkout Service has zero endpoints, and callers get connection refused. Frontend spans show POST /api/checkout failing with HTTP 500 and gRPC status 14 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.197.76:8080' (10.96.197.76 is the checkout ClusterIP), and the frontend pod log repeats the same refusal. The pod template was changed at 03:24:23 by a kubectl-client-side-apply on Deployment checkout (generation 1 -> 2; last-applied annotation contains nodeSelector extra-node) while the previous checkout pod, scheduled at 03:23:41 on sregym-worker and running its checkout container since 03:24:06, was killed at 03:24:23. A second update by manager OpenAPI-Generator at 03:24:29 also changed PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR to product-catalog:8082, a port the product-catalog Service does not expose (8080 only); that is a second candidate defect on the same object whose effect is not yet observable because no checkout pod has been scheduled. All other 23 deployments in astronomy-shop have one available replica and no nodeSelector; no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota exists; Prometheus history is effectively absent (single sample at 03:24:40), so no trend or exact onset can be established from metrics.

claims.text: Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} and status replicas=2, unavailableReplicas=2, readyReplicas=null, availableReplicas=null, observedGeneration=2.
The cluster has exactly four nodes with hostnames sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3; no node carries the hostname extra-node.
Among the 23 Deployments in astronomy-shop, only checkout has a non-null nodeSelector/affinity; the other 22 have nodeSelector null and one available replica each.

Both checkout pods, checkout-54579c864c-xwx7z and checkout-c69887c97-jb9z2, are Pending with PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable and message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
kube_pod_status_unschedulable is 1 for checkout-54579c864c-xwx7z and checkout-c69887c97-jb9z2, and kube_pod_status_phase Pending is 1 / Running 0 for both at 03:24:40.
Endpoints object 'checkout' in astronomy-shop has no subsets and no addresses, while all 22 other Services in the namespace have ready addresses.
kube_deployment_status_replicas_available reports 0 for deployment checkout at 03:24:40, while every other deployment in astronomy-shop reports 1.

Frontend error spans show POST /api/checkout (server, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (500), and client span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and exception message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.197.76:8080 (2026-11-24T03:24:32.690Z)', plus tcp.connect spans with otel.status_description 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.197.76:8080'.
The checkout Service clusterIP is 10.96.197.76 with port 8080, so the refused address in the frontend spans and logs is the checkout Service.

frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-jnfxp logged 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.197.76:8080' at 03:24:07.662Z, 03:24:32.690Z (and earlier refusals to cart 10.96.243.211:8080 at 03:23:52 and ad 10.96.27.59:8080 at 03:23:56).

Warning events FailedScheduling were recorded for pod checkout-54579c864c-xwx7z at 2026-11-24T03:24:23Z and for pod checkout-c69887c97-jb9z2 at 2026-11-24T03:24:29Z with the same 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' message.

Deployment checkout metadata.managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 03:23:41Z, kubectl-client-side-apply Update at 03:24:23Z and OpenAPI-Generator Update at 03:24:29Z, and its kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration recorded at 03:24:23Z contains nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} together with PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080 (all other deployments show only a helm Apply from 03:23:41Z).

The previous checkout pod checkout-6c769b88b5-4r47c was Scheduled to sregym-worker at 03:23:41Z, started its checkout container at 03:24:06Z, and received a Normal 'Killing - Stopping container checkout' event at 03:24:23Z.

Two ReplicaSets owned by Deployment checkout exist: checkout-54579c864c (created 03:24:23Z, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080, nodeSelector extra-node) and checkout-c69887c97 (created 03:24:29Z, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082, nodeSelector extra-node); the live Deployment template now carries product-catalog:8082.

The product-catalog Service exposes only port 8080 (targetPort 8080) and the product-catalog pod's container port is 8080 named 'service', so PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082 in the checkout template points to a port that is not exposed.

The frontend span-metric series 'traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",span_name="POST /api/checkout",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}' exists for the window, evidencing frontend errors on the checkout route.

Jaeger's service list for this target contains ad, cart, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation; checkout is not among them, consistent with checkout having produced no server-side spans.

Resource shortage and quota are not the cause of the Pending checkout pods: the scheduler message cites node affinity/selector mismatch (not insufficient cpu/memory), and astronomy-shop contains no ResourceQuota objects.

Rejected: that a NetworkPolicy blocks traffic into the checkout Service. astronomy-shop contains no NetworkPolicy objects, and the checkout Service has no endpoints at all, so the refusals are a no-endpoint condition rather than a policy drop.

Rejected: that cart and ad are the fault. Their refusals in the frontend log occurred at 03:23:52Z/03:23:56Z during initial startup, and both Services currently have ready endpoints (cart 10.244.7.240, ad 10.244.7.223).

The change that broke checkout was the kubectl-client-side-apply to Deployment checkout at 03:24:23Z that introduced nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node: it created ReplicaSet checkout-54579c864c, the previously running pod checkout-6c769b88b5-4r47c was killed at the same second, and every replacement pod has been Unschedulable since.

A second, independent defect candidate remains on the same object: the 03:24:29Z OpenAPI-Generator update left PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082, which does not match the product-catalog Service port 8080. Its effect is not yet observable because no checkout pod has been scheduled, but it would break checkout-to-product-catalog calls once scheduling is fixed.

Recommend correcting Deployment checkout (astronomy-shop) so its pod template no longer selects the non-existent node kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node (remove the nodeSelector or set it to an existing hostname such as sregym-worker/sregym-worker2/sregym-worker3), and simultaneously correct PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR back to product-catalog:8080, then confirm both checkout pods become Running/Ready and that Endpoints 'checkout' gains an address.

gaps: No metric history is available: every kube_* and traces_span_metrics series returned a single sample at 2026-11-24T03:24:40Z (source_start_at equals the window end), so no baseline or trend exists and the exact onset cannot be timed from metrics; the timeline rests on Kubernetes events and the last-applied annotation.

managedFieldsSummary gives only manager and time (kubectl-client-side-apply 03:24:23Z, OpenAPI-Generator 03:24:29Z) and not which fields each write changed; which update added the nodeSelector and which changed PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR cannot be proven directly.

The pre-change ReplicaSet checkout-6c769b88b5 no longer exists, so its pod template (previous nodeSelector and PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR values) cannot be read; the inference that extra-node was not present before 03:24:23 rests on the last-applied annotation content plus the 03:23:41 Scheduled / 03:24:06 Started / 03:24:23 Killing events of that pod.
No change_history integration is configured, so no audit of who or what applied the checkout changes, and no chaos/fault-injection object was observed holding these settings.

No checkout server-side traces or logs exist for the incident (the old pod is gone, new pods never started), so the checkout-side failure is only visible through its absence of endpoints and caller-side refusals.
Traces are a Jaeger in-memory sample (most recent traces); the frontend error view is a biased sample, not a failure rate.

A DaemonSet otel-collector-agent rollout replaced agent pods at ~03:24:12-03:24:16Z (3 SuccessfulDelete, 6 SuccessfulCreate events; old pods 4vqpz/9g8t4/f4hxc killed) and span-metric counters restarted at 03:24:40Z; its trigger was not determined and it is not shown to be related to the checkout outage.

Other transient noise not tied to this cause: FailedMount 'failed to sync configmap cache' warnings at 03:23:42Z, startup probe misses on opensearch-0 and grafana, and a PodDisruptionBudget NoPods event; none of these objects currently shows failure.
next_steps: Inspect and correct the checkout Deployment pod template (nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname and PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR) and verify scheduling, readiness and Service endpoints afterwards.
Identify the client behind the kubectl-client-side-apply and OpenAPI-Generator writes to Deployment checkout (audit log or change history) to confirm the injected change and prevent recurrence.
After checkout is schedulable, re-check checkout-to-product-catalog calls for connection errors on port 8082 to confirm or refute the second defect candidate.
Establish Prometheus history (or a comparable baseline window) so future incidents can be timed and trended rather than judged from a single scrape.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
